title: Catch phishing in Teams chats: ZAP for Teams, QR-code URL detection and user reporting
problem: Since early October 2026 (rollout completes early November), Defender for Office 365 also extracts the URLs hidden in QR codes in Teams messages after delivery and puts a warning on malicious ones. With ZAP for Teams on, eligible malicious internal messages can be blocked.
steps: Microsoft Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration > Microsoft Teams protection (security.microsoft.com/securitysettings/teamsProtectionPolicy): check that the Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP) toggle is On.
On the same page, pick the quarantine policies for malware and high-confidence phishing, and add exclusions only if you really need them. Exclusions apply to recipients, not senders.
PowerShell alternative: `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy | Format-List Name,ZapEnabled` and `Set-TeamsProtectionPolicy -Identity "Teams Protection Policy" -ZapEnabled $true`.

Turn on user reporting in two places: 'Report a security concern' in the Teams admin center messaging policies (plus calling and meeting reporting if you want them), and 'Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams' on the Teams user reported settings page (security.microsoft.com/securitysettings/teamsUserSubmission). Existing tenants need to enable the Defender setting themselves.
Hunt for QR-code detections in Advanced Hunting: `MessageUrlInfo | where UrlLocation == "QRCode"`.
Tell the SOC that users can now also report Teams calls, meetings and meeting participants, so these reports show up on the Submissions page.
pitfalls: ZAP for Teams and Safe Links for Teams need Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or higher, which Microsoft 365 E3 has included since July 2026. Advanced hunting on Teams messages needs Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5.
ZAP for Teams quarantines only internal chats and channels, and only for malware and high-confidence phishing.
Quarantined Teams messages are currently admin-only, and users get no quarantine notifications.
User reporting in Teams isn't supported in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
done_when: 'Report a security concern' is on in Teams messaging policies and 'Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams' is on in Defender.
The SOC has a saved hunting query for QR-code URLs in Teams.

troubleshooting.symptom: `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy` or the ZAP toggle is not available
troubleshooting.cause: The tenant has no Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or higher
troubleshooting.fix: Check the licence (Microsoft 365 E3 includes Plan 1 since July 2026); advanced hunting on Teams messages additionally needs Plan 2 or E5.

troubleshooting.symptom: A phishing message from an external chat was not removed
troubleshooting.cause: ZAP for Teams acts only on internal chats and channels, and only for malware and high-confidence phishing
troubleshooting.fix: Handle external-chat threats through Teams external access/federation settings and user reporting; do not expect ZAP to cover them.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users ask where a removed message went and got no notice
troubleshooting.cause: Quarantined Teams messages are admin-only and users get no quarantine notification
troubleshooting.fix: Review and release from Quarantine in the Defender portal; tell the service desk this is expected behaviour.

troubleshooting.symptom: 'Report a security concern' is missing in Teams
troubleshooting.cause: Only one of the two settings is on, or the tenant is GCC/GCC High/DoD
troubleshooting.fix: Enable it in the Teams messaging policy and turn on 'Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams' in Defender; user reporting is not supported in government clouds.

rollback: If ZAP for Teams quarantines legitimate internal content, add a targeted recipient exclusion in the Teams protection policy rather than turning ZAP off.

Last resort: `Set-TeamsProtectionPolicy -Identity "Teams Protection Policy" -ZapEnabled $false`, then confirm with `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy | Format-List Name,ZapEnabled`, and record an end date for re-enabling.
User reporting can be switched off again in the Teams messaging policy and on the Teams user reported settings page; existing submissions stay on the Submissions page.

history.note: Added troubleshooting (licensing, external chats, admin-only quarantine, missing report button) and rollback, derived from the documented limitations.
